security_spec.violation_condition: If FreeBSD kernel or bhyve VMM implements xiselect/xireg indirect CSR emulation and uses the pre-fix upper bound of 0x1100 (inclusive) instead of 0x10FF (inclusive) for the ACLIC reserved-raise-illegal range, then xiselect=0x1100 accessing xireg4/xireg5/xireg6 will silently read/write undefined microarchitectural state instead of raising an illegal instruction trap, either in the kernel itself or in a bhyve guest escaping virtualization boundaries
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD has no xiselect/xireg implementation yet, but any future kernel CLIC/SMIDCSR emulation or bhyve virtualized CSRs using the old 0x1100 inclusive bound would fail to trap xiselect=0x1100 as illegal, leaking reserved state

findings.finding: No xiselect/xireg indirect CSR emulation exists in the kernel trap handler. Illegal instruction exceptions (SCAUSE_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION) unconditionally panic the kernel rather than attempting CSR emulation, so no speculative CSR range bounds bug can exist here.
User-mode illegal instruction handler only checks for FPE lazy save/restore; no indirect CSR (xiselect/xireg) emulation implemented. Unknown CSRs in userspace correctly generate SIGILL.

bhyve VMM only saves/restores standard supervisor CSRs (vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp). No siselect/sireg or xiselect/xireg indirect CSR access is virtualized. No Smcsrind or SmIdctrl ISA extension support.

Guest virtual instruction traps (SCAUSE_VIRTUAL_INSTRUCTION) only handle WFI; no smcsrind/smstateen/smidctrl CSR virtualization. Unrecognized virtual instructions result in VM_EXITCODE_BOGUS, safely passing to userland.

RISC-V CSR definitions in this header include only standard privilege CSRs (sstatus, sie, stvec, satp, etc.) plus hypervisor CSRs (hstatus, hvip, hie, etc.). No siselect/sireg (0x150/0x151), miselect/mireg (0x350/0x351), or xiselect/xireg CSR definitions exist.

The only 'select/data' register pairs defined are the Sdtrig debug trigger CSRs (tselect=0x7a0, tdata1-3=0x7a1-0x7a3). These are entirely separate from the xiselect/xireg indirect CSR extension. No bounds-checking bug relevant to the security spec exists.
